proposal.summary: Created three local memory entries capturing the user's MATLAB temporary-employment model structure, the plan shift to GMM estimation of dshape/dscale/fc/cc, and the CSV data format (y, stockP, stockT).
proposal.rationale: The trajectory (user messages m_0004:0 and m_0006:0, dated 2023-11-08) directly establishes durable project facts: the model's equations for lambdap, lambdat, stockP, and stockT from the user's own code; the user's stated plan change from pre-decided dshape, dscale, fc, cc values to estimating them via GMM against observed data; and the CSV data schema with one stockP and stockT observation per productivity value y. The existing harness has no entries for this research project, so new memory entries are warranted. No prior refinement history exists, so no rollbacks are needed. Per instructions, edits are memory-only with cited sourceIds; assistant-origin code (m_0001:0, m_0005:0) is cited only as supporting context for the code draft and adopted CSV-reading approach, with the substantive facts anchored in user statements.

edits.title: Temporary employment regulation model: MATLAB code structure for thresholds and job stocks (2023-11-08)
edits.content: As of 2023-11-08, the user is developing MATLAB code for a research model titled 'Temporary Employment, Firm Heterogeneity and Regulation'. Per user-provided code: lambdap(i) = (y(i) - r*U - r*cc)/(cc + fc) for each productivity value y; lambdat(i) is solved numerically via csolve on eval_lambdat(lambda, cc, U, fc, r, y(i)); stockP(i) = integral over [1e-8, lambdap(i)] of (1/lambda) .* jobsP, where jobsP = G(lambdap(i), dscale, dshape) - G(1e-8, dscale, dshape); stockT(i) = integral over [lambdap(i), lambdat(i)] of (1/lambda) .* log(y(i)/(r*U)) .* jobsT, where jobsT = G(lambdat(i), dscale, dshape) - G(lambdap(i), dscale, dshape). G is the CDF of the distribution of shock arrival rates; the code draft selects the Weibull law. The code draft also computes a conversion threshold lambdas via fzero on eval_lambdas and uses r_annual = 0.05 (converted to a daily rate), log-normal productivity (mu = log(1.57), sigma = 0.1, n = 10000 draws), U = 1/r, and pre-decided values dscale = 0.02, dshape = 1.1, fc = 50, cc = 0.0020 (parameter values per the rewritten code draft, not independently confirmed by the user).
edits.reason: Records the model's equations and code organization from the user's own code so future sessions can continue the project without re-deriving the structure.

edits.title: dshape, dscale, fc, and cc now to be estimated via GMM instead of pre-decided values (2023-11-08)
edits.content: Plan change stated by the user on 2023-11-08 for the temporary employment model: they had been working with pre-decided values for dshape, dscale, fc, and cc, but now want to estimate these four parameters using GMM to match values observed in the data. In the data, the user observes stockP and stockT for each productivity value y. This entry records the updated estimation plan replacing the earlier fixed-parameter approach. This is a stated goal at the time of the conversation; no completed estimation results were reported.
edits.reason: Captures the mid-project shift from fixed parameters to GMM estimation as a separate dated entry, per the update policy, so later questions about the current estimation approach can be answered correctly.

edits.title: Model data CSV with columns y, stockP, stockT; one stockP and stockT observation per y value (2023-11-08)
edits.content: For the temporary employment model's GMM estimation, the user's observations are stored in a CSV file with three columns: y (productivity), stockP (observed stock of permanent jobs), and stockT (observed stock of temporary jobs); for each y value there corresponds exactly one stockP and one stockT observation. On 2023-11-08 the user requested code to load this CSV; the adopted approach reads it with data = readmatrix('data.csv') and extracts y = data(:,1), stockP_obs = data(:,2), stockT_obs = data(:,3) (assistant-proposed code that the user then asked to have integrated into the full model). The user asked for the rest of the model code to be rewritten to use these observed arrays in place of the previously simulated y values.
edits.reason: Records the input data schema and loading convention so future work on the GMM estimation knows the exact column layout and one-observation-per-y structure.

proposal.expectedOutcome: Future sessions continuing this temporary employment regulation project can recall the model's threshold and stock equations, the GMM estimation goal for the four parameters, and the input CSV column layout (y, stockP, stockT) without re-deriving them from scratch. Validate by checking that follow-up questions about the model, estimation, or data loading are answered consistently with these recorded facts, and that any later change in parameter values or estimation approach is captured as a new separate entry.
